content:
Facts: Testator disposed all real estate via holographic will assigning specific assets to nephews (children of predeceased siblings); beneficiaries contested whether provisions constituted legacies versus institutions ex re certa; claimed division of undisposed movable assets (bank deposits, securities, jewellery) among testamentary heirs proportionally to bequeathed property values versus legitimate succession for siblings; disputes arose over property identification errors, items found in apartment safe, expropriation compensation allocation, and credit joint ownership characterization.
Legal Framework: Articles 457(2), 588, 734, 737 Italian Civil Code (legitimate-testamentary succession concurrence; institutio ex re certa distinction; inter liberos division; collation); Arts. 588(2), 655, 674(2) (universal versus particular dispositions; bequest scope; accretion); Arts. 727, 752, 754, 757, 760 (inheritance credits non-automatic division; inheritance costs allocation).
Interpretive Issues: Distinguishing institutio ex re certa from legacy when testator assigns all specific real assets exhausting property without abstract share reference; whether "expansive force" extends institutions to unknown/supervening assets versus only assets testator knowingly omitted; scope of inter liberos division when objectively partial; interpretation of dwelling bequest "with everything inside" regarding valuables; joint versus divisible credit characterization for assets collectively apportioned by testator; lineage versus capita division when textual ambiguity exists.
Principles Applied: Article 588(2) requires subjective assessment of testator's intent whether specific-asset assignment constitutes share-based institution. No predetermined criteria distinguish institutio ex re certa from legacy; trial judge's factual determination unassailable if adequately justified. Testator assigning all specific real assets to nephews while explicitly reserving movable distribution to non-testamentary acts (evidenced by: will preamble stating intent to "dispose of assets"; exhaustion of considerable real estate; extrajudicial statements revealing exclusion intent toward siblings; sealed safe deposit box note contemplating private distributions; testamentary clause acknowledging unallocated expropriation compensation) establishes institutions ex re certa with shares calculated ex post as ratio between bequeathed value and total estate value at succession opening. "Expansive force" theory inapplicable to knowingly omitted assets; Art. 457(2) governs legitimate succession concurrence for assets testator deliberately excluded from will intending alternative disposition. Inter liberos division per Art. 734 may coincide with institutions ex re certa when simultaneously establishing heirs and dividing estate; Art. 734(2) incorporates Art. 457(2) principle requiring legitimate succession for objectively partial divisions absent contrary testator intent validly expressed. Dwelling bequest scope determined at succession opening absent temporal limitation indication; "everything inside" encompasses all items permanently kept including personal effects, valuables, everyday jewelry, distinguishable from bank-stored catalogued items. Collective undivided asset apportionment creates joint ownership distinct from inheritance community; originates from testator's dispositive act, not succession. Collectively apportioned credits (expropriation compensation) automatically divided since inception among designated creditors per testamentary proportions; each holds individual claim against debtor. Division clause designating manager operative only during joint ownership persistence; dissolves upon termination. Expression ambiguity resolved through overall will examination, lineage consideration patterns, predecessor-descendant indication structure, share-number correspondence, beneficiary understanding evidenced in positions.
